title: A remark on the log-Sobolev inequality for the Gibbs measure of the focusing Schrodinger equation: the spectral-gap criterion for the truncated Gibbs measure (printed as Proposition 4.6)
author: Guopeng Li, Jiawei Li, Leonardo Tolomeo
work: A remark on the log-Sobolev inequality for the Gibbs measure of the focusing Schrodinger equation
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Proposition 4.6 (source0.tex lines 1589--1610, source label s4:PROP:crit), the quantitative criterion that turns smallness of three explicit quantities into a bound on the Hessian of the renormalised potential against the Gaussian covariance term, which is the step the paper's log-Sobolev conclusion rests on. It is delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 1612--1690 (79 lines, one adjacent proof environment, no gap and no deferral) and with the six labelled statements it invokes. The proof is a genuine quantitative argument: it first controls the auxiliary parameter of the recentred field through the exponential-moment lemma, then combines the recentring lemma, Taylor's formula with its remainder bound and the two-sided bound for the weighted Hessian to show that the Hessian of the renormalised potential differs from the reference quadratic form by a factor controlled by the small parameter, and finally evaluates the resulting ratio along the recentred field and closes the estimate with the Gaussian lemma. The substantive steps are the comparison of the two quadratic forms with explicit constants and the passage from the renormalised potential to the truncated Gibbs measure. H3: a complete original research-paper proof of the paper's central quantitative criterion, with every invoked lemma delivered.
